United India Insuranceco.Ltd vs Paul Abraham on 7 August, 2025

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the second respondent/insurer in O.P. (MV) No.351/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Perumbavoor (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 24/09/2019.
The respondent herein is the claim petitioner in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 31/12/2015 at about 04:45 p.m., while he was walking through Muvattupuzha- Ernakulam road, car bearing registration No.KL-40/C-5613, driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner rammed motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-07/BB-1896 going in front of the car as a result of which the motorcycle hit him and he sustained 2025:KER:59415 grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/owner-cum-driver remained ex parte.
4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/owner-cum-driver.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Exts.A1 to A22 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent/owner-cum-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 51,02,391- together with interest @ 8%
per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the second respondent/insurer has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this 2025:KER:59415 appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the second respondent/insurer that the percentage of disability fixed as 17% by the Tribunal is on the higher side in the light of the injury sustained by the claim petitioner, which is quite mild.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the Tribunal has given cogent reasons for fixing the disability at 17% which suffers from no infirmity and hence, no interference is called for.
10.

Ext.A7 wound certificate shows that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Conscious, Oriented, pain low back, tenderness over L2 region, C.T.Scan Spine-minimal comminuted fracture L2, vertibral body superior end plate anteriorly.
No spinal canal compromise at that level.

Had consultation with Dept. of Spine Surgery Treated as out patient with advise for review and MRI Scan L.S.Spine."
11. Exhibit A8 treatment cum discharge summary read thus:

PHYSICAL FINDIGNS BP - 110/80 mm HG Pr., Temp:Normal.
 Tenderness:+++ (Lumbar  region), SLR:-VE (Both legs),
 Power of U/L/L: Good, Blader  & bowel Good control.
 INVESTIGATION
All lab reports are attached.
MRI L S Spine (Self)-Showes  Mild compression fracture of L2  Vertebral body.
DIAGNOSIS Compression#L2 spine.

TREATMENT SUMMARY Snehavasthy-4 days,
 Immobilization with Lumbar  POP on 2.1.16.
CONDITION ON DISCHARGE Discharge with Lumbar POP.

RECOMMENDATIONS 1. Advised to take rest for 40 days 2.Continue medicines as prescribed 3. Consult the OPD after 40 days for POP cast removal and for follow up treatment"

sentences.text: Ext.A16 disability certificate has been issued by a private doctor and the doctor who issued the certificate was not examined for proving the contents of Ext.A16, though its marking was objected to by the second respondent/insurer.
That being the position, the Tribunal was right in not relying completely on Ext.A16 to fix the disability percentage.
However, the fact that the accident occurred and that the claim petitioner sustained the aforesaid injuries is not disputed.
That being the position, I find that the disability percentage can be fixed as 15% taking into account the injuries sustained.
